direction: Blend dimensionless mean-isolation farness with linear destination (closing) pull in the next-node score, keeping the step O(n) vectorized so remaining budget is spent on better choices rather than lookahead.

operations.mechanism: Archive shows the current best solver (93030.89 mean, 6.68 ms) is still ~0.46% off VBS and weakest at size 50/100/200, where NN-family constructions leave long late edges. KB entry method-tsp-i605-mean-farness reports mean-isolation farness as the best-performing fully-completing island rule (all 128 completed), method-tsp-i605-dest-pull shows the linear destination-pull form is algebraically a vectorized regret/insertion hybrid running at sub-millisecond cost, and method-tsp-i605-dimensionless-ratio shows max-normalized dimensionless features give strict scale invariance and full completion. Because both signals are O(n) per candidate step (O(n^2)-O(n^3) per instance) and our current solve time is only ~6.7 ms of a 500 ms budget, we can afford the richer score without any completion risk, and the per-step max-normalization keeps the two weights meaningful across the heterogeneous coordinate scales in the 36-instance suite.

preserve: Route feasibility, strict time budget, and scale invariance.
hypothesis: Scoring candidate u from current node c as score(u) = d(c,u)/max_d - w_f * mean_{v unvisited}(d(v,u))/max_mean + w_d * d(u,start)/max_d (all terms divided by their current-step maximum, so the rule is scale-invariant) yields shorter tours than plain nearest-neighbour while staying well inside the 500 ms budget; the mean-farness term counteracts NN's early 'stranding' of isolated cities and the destination-pull term truncates the long closing edge, so the combined score should beat either alone, especially on the size=100/200 regimes where the archived portfolio shows the largest gaps.
